name: Uber
summary: Mobility platform. Bold black and white, tight type, urban energy
description: An inspired interpretation of Uber's design language — a transportation-and-delivery super-app brand whose web surface is a black-and-white duet, framed by a custom geometric display sans, accented by a single signature pill shape (radius 999px) on every interactive element, and decorated only by editorial 4:3 illustrations of riders, drivers, and city objects.

colors.name: Ink Black
colors.role: The brand's only conversion colour. Every primary CTA pill, the footer fill, every dark promo band, every nav login button. The system has no secondary accent.

colors.name: Surface Pressed
colors.role: The pressed-state fill for white pills — a soft grey that's used only in active / pressed states.

colors.name: Black Elevated
colors.role: A near-black used on hover for the translucent white tab-toggle pill. Documented as a system colour because it appears on a recurring brand control.

colors.name: Canvas Soft
colors.role: The soft gray fill for category chips, form-input rows inside the ride-request card, and subtle pill buttons.

colors.name: Canvas Softer
colors.role: A slightly lighter gray used as a nested-input fill on white surfaces.

colors.name: Ink
colors.role: Every heading and body paragraph on light surfaces.

colors.name: Body
colors.role: Secondary text — captions, sub-headings, supporting copy.

colors.name: Hairline Mid
colors.role: A mid-gray used for muted link text inside footer columns and breadcrumb-style nav.

colors.name: Mute
colors.role: The lightest text role — placeholder text, fine print, low-priority metadata.

colors.name: On Dark
colors.role: All text on `{colors.ink}` surfaces (footer, dark promo bands).

substitutesNote:
The two faces are proprietary. Open-source substitutes:
- **Display sans** — *Inter* weight 700 with `font-feature-settings: "ss01"` enabled comes closest. *Geist* weight 700 is the second-best option.
- **Text sans** — *Inter* weights 400 / 500 match the geometric width and x-height. *Plus Jakarta Sans* is a softer alternative if the brand wants a less neutral feel.
